theorem map_smul'' (f : M →ₗ[R] M') : (I • N).map f = I • N.map f :=
  le_antisymm
    (map_le_iff_le_comap.2 <|
      smul_le.2 fun r hr n hn =>
        show f (r • n) ∈ I • N.map f from
          (f.map_smul r n).symm ▸ smul_mem_smul hr (mem_map_of_mem hn)) <|
    smul_le.2 fun r hr _ hn =>
      let ⟨p, hp, hfp⟩ := mem_map.1 hn
      hfp ▸ f.map_smul r p ▸ mem_map_of_mem (smul_mem_smul hr hp)

C1_dependencies.name: rfl
C1_dependencies.content:
/--
`rfl : a = a` is the unique constructor of the equality type. This is the
same as `Eq.refl` except that it takes `a` implicitly instead of explicitly.

This is a more powerful theorem than it may appear at first, because although
the statement of the theorem is `a = a`, Lean will allow anything that is
definitionally equal to that type. So, for instance, `2 + 2 = 4` is proven in
Lean by `rfl`, because both sides are the same up to definitional equality.
-/
@[match_pattern] def rfl {α : Sort u} {a : α} : Eq a a := Eq.refl a

theorem isUnit_iff {z : ℤ_[p]} : IsUnit z ↔ ‖z‖ = 1 :=
  ⟨fun h => by
    rcases isUnit_iff_dvd_one.1 h with ⟨w, eq⟩
    refine le_antisymm (norm_le_one _) ?_
    have := mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_left (norm_le_one w) (norm_nonneg z)
    rwa [mul_one, ← norm_mul, ← eq, norm_one] at this, fun h =>
    ⟨⟨z, z.inv, mul_inv h, inv_mul h⟩, rfl⟩⟩

informal_statement: For any element \( x \) in the normed ring of integers localized at prime \( p \) (denoted \( \mathbb{Z}_{[p]} \)) and any natural number \( n \), the norm of \( x \) raised to the power \( n \) is equal to the norm of \( x \) raised to the power \( n \). In other words, \( \|x^n\|_+ = \|x\|_+^n \).
informal_proof: The statement asserts that the norm of a power of an element is equal to the power of its norm. This can be proven by leveraging the properties of norms in a normed ring. Specifically, the norm function respects multiplication and powers, meaning that \( \|xy\|_+ = \|x\|_+ \cdot \|y\|_+ \) for any elements \( x \) and \( y \) in the ring. Applying this property iteratively, we find that \( \|x^n\|_+ = \|x\|_+^n \). This follows directly from the definition and properties of the norm function, confirming the equality in the theorem.

protected lemma nnnorm_pow (x : ℤ_[p]) (n : ℕ) : ‖x ^ n‖₊ = ‖x‖₊ ^ n := by simp [nnnorm, NNReal]

/-- Nonnegative real numbers, denoted as `ℝ≥0` withinin the NNReal namespace -/
def NNReal := { r : ℝ // 0 ≤ r } deriving
  Zero, One, Semiring, StrictOrderedSemiring, CommMonoidWithZero, CommSemiring,
  PartialOrder, SemilatticeInf, SemilatticeSup, DistribLattice, OrderedCommSemiring,
  OrderedCommMonoid, Nontrivial, Inhabited

C1_dependencies.name: nnnorm_pow
C1_dependencies.content:
@[simp]
theorem nnnorm_pow (a : α) (n : ℕ) : ‖a ^ n‖₊ = ‖a‖₊ ^ n :=
  (nnnormHom.toMonoidHom : α →* ℝ≥0).map_pow a n
